title: Guest Network Daily Consumption
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog, ISP uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=unifi:event
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(rx_bytes) as rx_bytes, sum(tx_bytes) as tx_bytes by network_name _time
| eval total_gb=round((rx_bytes+tx_bytes)/1073741824,2)
| where network_name="guest"
| sort - _time
description: Tracks how much traffic actually flows over the guest network each day, which is useful for capacity, courtesy, and spotting a guest SSID nobody needs anymore.
value: A dedicated guest network is good hygiene, but this metric shows whether it is a core part of your home or just configuration nostalgia.
implementation: Forward per-network traffic events from UniFi; review daily guest-SSID volume and right-size the network or QoS policies accordingly.
visualization: Daily chart of guest-network total traffic in gigabytes.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how much internet use is really happening on the guest Wi-Fi each day.
